title: AI PM Learning Roadmap
summary: AI product management requires mastery of nine distinct skill areas: prompt engineering, context engineering/RAG, AI prototyping, agentic workflows, evals and testing, foundation models, PRD frameworks, and career positioning. The roadmap positions these skills as more valuable than expensive courses and provides free tools and resources for each domain. Common mistakes in AI product building include lacking fallback strategies, ignoring latency and cost constraints, and overfitting to demos rather than rigorous evaluation.
central_argument: AI PM is a specialized subset of product management requiring technical depth in prompting, RAG, prototyping, and evaluation frameworks that can be self-taught through free resources more effectively than paid courses.
key_claims: AI PM is a subset of PM with the same core tasks but applied to AI features, products, and tools
Prompt engineering is the number-one skill for great agents and productivity
RAG should be used for retrieving specific knowledge or documents, prompting for simple instructions, and fine-tuning for specialized domains
Common AI product mistakes include building without evaluation frameworks, ignoring latency/cost, lacking fallback strategies, and overfitting to demos
Claude excels at reasoning and coding, GPT-4 is most versatile, and Gemini leads in multimodal capabilities
AI PM interviews test vibe coding ability and understanding of AI ethics and guardrails
key_tensions: The article argues against the necessity of expensive courses ($2k+) for learning AI PM, claiming free resources are superior
It complicates the assumption that traditional PM skills directly transfer to AI PM by emphasizing required technical depth
It pushes back on common AI product development approaches that lack proper evaluation, cost awareness, and fallback mechanisms
